cues.en: This episode of Real Engineering is brought to you by Brilliant, a problem solving website that teaches you to think like an engineer.
cues.zh: 本期 Real Engineering 由 Brilliant 赞助，它是一个教你像工程师一样思考的解题网站。

cues.en: Over the past decade we have seen multiple industries looking to transition to renewable fuel sources,
cues.zh: 过去十年，我们看到多个行业都在寻求转向可再生燃料来源，

cues.en: and while we have seen huge strides in production of renewable energy, the technology required to allow every industry to use it has not kept pace.
cues.zh: 尽管可再生能源生产取得了巨大进步，但让每个行业都能使用它的所需技术却没跟上。

cues.en: In theory we could replace every coal burning power plant in the world in the morning and manage just fine,
cues.zh: 理论上，我们可以在一个早上替换掉全世界所有燃煤电厂，还能运转得很好，

cues.en: if we had a reasonable way of storing that energy cost effectively and efficiently.
cues.zh: 前提是我们有一种合理的方式，能经济高效地储存这些能源。

cues.en: This energy storage dilemma is slowing our adoption of renewable energy, and one of the industries this is most apparent is the aviation and aerospace industry. Elon Musk is running around pushing electric vehicles and solar powered homes, yet every time a Falcon nine launches it burns 147
cues.zh: 这种储能困境正在拖慢我们对可再生能源的采用，而这一点最明显的行业之一就是航空与航天业。Elon Musk 到处推动电动汽车和太阳能住宅，可每次 Falcon 9 发射都会烧掉 147

cues.en: tons of fossil fuel. Boeing and Airbus are in a constant battle to create the most fuel efficient plane, allowing their customers to save on ever increasing fuel costs and increase their bottom line, yet they are still using kerosene when energy from the grid is cheaper. So what gives? Why isn't every industry on Earth clawing at the prospect of transitioning to renewable fuels? The aviation industry has one massive hurdle to overcome before it can successfully adopt renewable energy.
cues.zh: 吨化石燃料。Boeing 和 Airbus 一直在争夺造出最省油的飞机，让客户在日益上涨的燃料成本上省钱并提高利润，可他们仍在用煤油，而电网能源更便宜。那到底是怎么回事？为什么地球上不是每个行业都在争先恐后转向可再生燃料？航空业在成功采用可再生能源之前，还有一个巨大障碍要跨越。

cues.en: The energy density of our storage methods.
cues.zh: 我们各种储能方式的能量密度。

cues.en: Energy density is the measure of the energy we can harness from one kilogram of an energy source. For Kerrison, the fuel jet airliners use is about 43 MJkg.
cues.zh: 能量密度衡量的是我们从 1 千克能源中能获取多少能量。作为对比，喷气式客机使用的燃料约为 43 MJ/kg。

cues.en: Currently even our best lithium ion batteries come in around one MJkg,
cues.zh: 目前，即使最好的锂离子电池也只有大约 1 MJ/kg，

cues.en: so battery energy is over 40 times heavier than jet fuel. So why is this such a huge problem? A plane flies when lift equals the weight of the plane. So when we increase the weight we have to increase the lift, which requires more power. Needing more power means we need more batteries, which increases the weight again. We could end the video there, but going by the demographic breakdown of this channel we can go a little deeper.
cues.zh: 所以同样能量下，电池要比航空燃油重 40 多倍。那为什么这是个大问题？飞机在升力等于自身重量时飞行。所以重量增加，我们就得增加升力，而这需要更多动力。需要更多动力就意味着需要更多电池，这又进一步增加重量。视频本可以到这里结束，但看看本频道的观众构成，我们可以再深入一点。

cues.en: To understand why this is such a difficult problem let's do some back of the envelope calculations to convert two planes, the Airbus A320
cues.zh: 为了理解为什么这个问题如此困难，我们先做个粗略估算，把两架飞机——Airbus A320

cues.en: and a small personal aircraft like a Cessna to battery power.
cues.zh: 以及像Cessna这样的小型私人飞机——改成电池动力。

cues.en: Ultimately we want to know the power requirements of flight and how it will draw on the energy supply of the battery.
cues.zh: 最终我们想知道飞行需要多少功率，以及它会如何消耗电池的能量供应。

cues.en: The Work Energy Theorem tells us that work equals force by delta x, where delta x is the distance over which a force acts. Power is work per unit time, so p equals work divided by time.
cues.zh: 功-能定理告诉我们，功等于力乘以Δx，其中Δx是力作用的距离。功率是单位时间做的功，所以P等于功除以时间。

cues.en: Inserting our equation for work we get an equation for power that equals force multiplied by the distance divided by time, otherwise known as velocity.
cues.zh: 把功的公式代入，就得到功率公式：力乘以距离再除以时间，而距离除以时间就是速度。

cues.en: Here delta v is the velocity of whatever is getting worked on, in this case it's the air.
cues.zh: 这里的 Δv 是被做功物体的速度，这里就是空气。

cues.en: When a plane is flying at a constant height we know that the force of lift and the force of gravity are balanced. That means the upward force of lift has to be equal to the magnitude of the downward pull of gravity, which equals the mass of the plane multiplied by gravity. So the power required for lift equals the mass of the plane multiplied by gravity and delta v. The question is, what is delta v? It's the downward velocity of the air that the plane pushes downward,
cues.zh: 当飞机在恒定高度飞行时，我们知道升力和重力是平衡的。也就是说，向上的升力必须等于向下重力的量值，而重力等于飞机质量乘以重力加速度。所以，升力所需的功率等于飞机质量乘以重力加速度再乘以 Δv。问题是，Δv 是什么？它是飞机向下推的空气的向下速度，

cues.en: so let's call it delta v z. To find its value we have to think about the mechanism of lift. The lift an airplane provides is equal to the rate it delivers downward momentum to the air it displaces.
cues.zh: 那我们把它叫作 Δv_z。要算出它的值，就得考虑升力的产生机制。飞机提供的升力，等于它向所排开的空气传递向下动量的速率。

cues.en: This means that the force of gravity must be equal in magnitude to the downward velocity of the deflected air times the rate at which air gets deflected.
cues.zh: 这意味着重力的大小必须等于被偏转空气的下向速度乘以空气被偏转的速率。

cues.en: The mass of the air that the plane affects is simply the volume of the cylinder that it sweeps out per unit time times the density of the air.
cues.zh: 飞机所影响的空气质量，就是它单位时间内扫出的圆柱体积乘以空气密度。

cues.en: If we call the relevant cross sectional area a sweep then the volume it sweeps out per unit time is a sweep times the velocity of the plane. Therefore the mass flow rate equals the density of air times the cross sectional area times the velocity of the plane.
cues.zh: 如果我们把相关横截面积称为 a sweep，那么它单位时间扫出的体积就是 a sweep 乘以飞机速度。因此质量流量等于空气密度乘以横截面积再乘以飞机速度。

cues.en: Now the only outstanding quantity that we don't know is the area of air affected by the plane, a sweep. This isn't the cross sectional area of the plane, it's the area of influence the plane has on the surrounding air. This changes with the relative velocity of the plane and the air around it, but at cruising speed the plane dissipates vortices that have roughly the radius of the length of the plane's wings. Approximating this circle as a square, because we don't have enough ridiculous assumptions in this calculation,
cues.zh: 现在唯一还不知道的量，是飞机影响的空气面积，也就是一片扫掠区域。这不是飞机的横截面积，而是飞机对周围空气的影响面积。它会随飞机与其周围空气的相对速度变化，但在巡航速度下，飞机耗散出的涡旋半径大致等于飞机机翼的长度。把这个圆近似成正方形，因为这个计算里的离谱假设还不够多，

cues.en: the relevant area becomes L2 at cruising speed.
cues.zh: 在巡航速度下，相关面积就变成 L²。

cues.en: Putting it all together we have the force lift needs to provide with this equation.
cues.zh: 综合起来，升力需要提供的力就由这个方程给出。

cues.en: This equation is simply telling us the plane is sweeping out a tube of air and shifting it downwards,
cues.zh: 这个方程只是告诉我们，飞机扫出一管空气，并把它向下推，

cues.en: and that downward acceleration of air is equal to the downward pull of gravity on the plane, so the plane avoids falling by constantly paying the tax of streaming momentum downward via the air. Rearranging this equation we can now solve for delta vz in terms of quantities we can easily measure, and plugging this into our power equation the power needed for lift is given by this equation.
cues.zh: 而空气向下的加速度等于重力对飞机的向下拉力，所以飞机通过不断让空气向下带走动量来“缴税”，从而避免下落。重新整理这个方程，就能用容易测量的量解出 delta vz；再把它代入功率方程，升力所需的功率就由这个方程给出。

cues.en: With this equation at hand we can start noticing what variables really impact the energy requirements on the plane. Notice that as the plane flies faster the power drawn by the engine actually gets smaller, but this equation neglects to consider drag. It just so happens that the total power needed to fly is minimized when the force of lift and the force of drag become equal. So we simply need to double our power requirements to get our total power requirement at cruising speed. Now we are getting a real picture of why increasing the mass of a plane is such a huge issue.
cues.zh: 有了这个方程，我们就可以开始看出哪些变量真正影响飞机的能量需求。注意，飞机飞得越快，发动机消耗的功率反而越小，但这个方程忽略了阻力。碰巧的是，当升力和阻力相等时，飞行所需的总功率会降到最低。所以我们只需把功率需求翻倍，就能得到巡航速度下的总功率需求。现在，我们真正看清了为什么增加飞机质量会是个大问题。

cues.en: The mass component of this equation is not only squared, but doubled.
cues.zh: 这个方程中的质量项不仅被平方，还被加倍。

cues.en: Doubling the mass will increase our power requirements eight fold. With this knowledge in hand, let's start calculating the real world consequences of converting an Airbus A320 and a Cessna to battery power.
cues.zh: 质量翻倍会使我们的功率需求增至原来的八倍。掌握了这一点，我们就来算算把一架空客 A320 和一架塞斯纳改装为电池动力，在现实世界中会带来什么后果。

cues.en: To start we can take the battery weight to be the usual mass fraction that's devoted to fuel, about 20% of the plane's mass for both. We also need to take into account the fact that at cruising altitude the atmosphere is much thinner than at ground level. For the Cessna the density falls by a factor of two and for the Airbus a factor of three. Let's be generous and take the specific power of leading edge lithium ion systems at about 0.34
cues.zh: 首先，我们可以把电池重量取为通常用于燃料的质量占比，两者都约为飞机质量的 20%。我们还需要考虑一个事实：在巡航高度，大气比地面稀薄得多。塞斯纳的密度降到二分之一，空客则降到三分之一。我们宽松一点，取先进锂离子系统的比功率约为 0.34

cues.en: kilowatts per kilogram. To meet the power demand the Airbus would need 31 tons of batteries, while the Cessna would need just 100 kilograms. For the Cessna this compares favorably with the typical weight of fuel it would carry otherwise and it isn't terrible for the Airbus, but this is just the power the plane needs at any one moment in time. What we are really interested in is the weight of batteries we would need to match the typical range of these planes. For the Airbus that's a seven hour flight from JFK to London Heathrow, and for the Cessna that might be a four hour flight from New York to South Carolina.
cues.zh: 千瓦每千克。为满足功率需求，空客需要 31 吨电池，而塞斯纳只需要 100 千克。对塞斯纳来说，这与它原本通常携带的燃油重量相比还算有利，对空客来说也不算太糟，但这只是飞机在任一时刻所需的功率。我们真正关心的是，要匹配这些飞机的典型航程，需要多重的电池。对空客来说，那是从 JFK 到伦敦希思罗的七小时飞行；对塞斯纳来说，可能是从纽约到南卡罗来纳的四小时飞行。

cues.en: The energy capacity required for a trip is given by this equation, multiplying the power required for flight by the duration of the flight. Again, if we use leading edge figures for lithium ion battery capacity
cues.zh: 一次飞行所需的能量容量由这个方程给出，即飞行所需功率乘以飞行时长。同样，如果我们采用锂离子电池容量的前沿数据

cues.en: we can store about two seventy eight watt hours per kilogram. For the Cessna the equivalent battery weight is just around 500 kilograms or just less than two thirds of the weight of the plane without fuel. For the A320 the required battery weight is about 260,000
cues.zh: 每公斤大约可以储存 278 瓦时。对于 Cessna，等效电池重量大约只有 500 公斤，略低于无燃料飞机重量的三分之二。对于 A320，所需电池重量约为 26 万

cues.en: kilograms or about four times the weight of the empty airplane.
cues.zh: 公斤，约为空机重量的四倍。

cues.en: Compared to the typical 20% that's allocated to fuel this is devastating.
cues.zh: 相比通常分配给燃料的20%，这简直是灾难性的。

cues.en: Now that we have a base figure for how heavy the batteries are going to be we can recalculate the actual range taking the added weight of the batteries into account. Let's assume at the very least we are not going to accept reduction in flight speed or increases in total energy used per flight.
cues.zh: 既然已有电池重量的基础估计，我们就可以把电池增加的重量算进去，重新计算实际航程。至少先假设，我们不接受飞行速度下降，也不接受每次飞行总能耗增加。

cues.en: How much is the range diminished for flights of similar speed and total energy? As expected, this downgrades the Cessna's flight time from four hours to about two hours, not negligible but livable. A two seater Cessna usually holds about 150 kilograms of fuel and another 100 kilograms for passengers and luggage. It is easy to imagine endowing the Cessna with the required battery capacity through a combination of lowering the carrying capacity, lowering speed, increasing wingspan,
cues.zh: 在相似速度和总能耗下，航程会缩短多少？如预期，这使Cessna的飞行时间从四小时降到约两小时，不可忽略但还能接受。双座Cessna通常携带约150公斤燃料，另有100公斤用于乘客和行李。很容易想象，通过降低载重、降低速度、增加翼展等组合，让Cessna具备所需电池容量，

cues.en: with lighter parts and more efficient electric engines.
cues.zh: 再加上更轻的部件和更高效的电动机。

cues.en: In fact this is exactly what we are seeing with small electric aircraft coming to market in the past few years like the Alpha Electro.
cues.zh: 事实上，过去几年像 Alpha Electro 这样进入市场的小型电动飞机，正是这种情况。

cues.en: However, the downgrade is substantial for the A320,
cues.zh: 然而，对 A320 来说，这种性能降级非常显著，

cues.en: taking us from seven hours down to just twenty minutes, less than one twentieth of the way across the Atlantic.
cues.zh: 使飞行时间从七小时降到仅仅二十分钟，还不到横跨大西洋航程的二十分之一。

cues.en: If we plot flight duration as a function of battery mass for both planes we can see that the Cessna is already sitting around the optimum and could actually increase our battery capacity and improve our flight range. It's a different story for the Airbus, where we overshot our optimum battery capacity significantly.
cues.zh: 如果把两架飞机的飞行时间作为电池质量的函数来绘图，就会发现 Cessna 已经接近最优值，实际上还能增加电池容量、提升航程。Airbus 则完全不同，我们的电池容量已经明显超过了最优值。

cues.en: Reducing our battery weight to 60 tons will increase our flight duration by about fifteen minutes, so we could last a little bit longer before crashing into the ocean, assuming we could find a place to fit those 60 tons of batteries in the first place. But we have been seeing great strides with short range small aircraft coming to market, and if we fly very slowly with low drag wings we can even build a solar powered drone that never has to land. We won't be seeing airliners using electric engines anytime soon, unless we can find a more energy dense medium for storing that energy. We will be exploring one such possibility in our next video, the truth about hydrogen. The derivations of the equations in this video may seem a little difficult to newcomers,
cues.zh: 把电池重量降到60吨，能让飞行时长增加约十五分钟，这样我们就能在坠入海洋前多撑一会儿——前提是我们首先找得到地方装下这60吨电池。但我们已经看到短程小型飞机在进入市场方面取得巨大进展；而且如果我们用低阻力机翼飞得很慢，甚至能造出永远不用降落的太阳能无人机。短期内不会看到客机使用电动发动机，除非我们能找到能量密度更高的储能介质。下期视频我们将探索这样一种可能性：氢的真相。本期视频中方程的推导对新手来说可能有点难，

cues.en: but if you follow along you will see that it's just taking basic known equations and combining them until we have a new equation that solves our problem. The value this skill will give you is immeasurable, but it takes practice.
cues.zh: 但如果你跟着做，就会发现，这不过是把已知的基本方程组合起来，直到得到一个能解决我们问题的新方程。这项技能带给你的价值无法估量，但需要练习。
